latency.source: docs/execution-evidence/agy-model-20261015/provider-calls.jsonl; pair dispatch.at -> finish.at; arithmetic mean of non-aborted successful finishes, rounded up to ms
limitations: Same plugin/model/medium and output limit 4096, earlier 120-second batch; present load may differ.
5 aborted calls are right-censored and excluded. Successful-call mean has survivor bias; future or incomplete calls can be slower.
Finish chunk precedes iterator settlement; provider preparation and host work are outside this interval. Explicit overhead reserve is required.
This is not 120 seconds divided by dispatch count, not modelDurationMs divided by attempts, and not a hard latency lower bound.

assumptions: Reference actions are a planning prior, never a strict model-call requirement.
Historical service latency is an explicit planning scenario, not a guaranteed future service bound.
Work/concurrency assumes full slot utilization; causal dependencies can reduce effective concurrency.
A scheduling shortfall can be remedied by either deadline or concurrency; the remedy label is explicit policy, not causal identification.
Admission permits an experiment; it does not guarantee success or completion within this allocation.

lowerBound.arithmetic: 4 distinct non-entry owners * (read decision + later evidence-send decision) + 2 entry checkpoint decisions = 10
assumptions: No guessed, hardcoded, prelearned or externally supplied hidden proofs; evidence is acquired through the advertised local read tool and directed mail.
A tool-call argument is fixed before its result is returned; no model consumes its own read result inside the same model response.
Phase-2 current evidence is read after checkpoint-only advancement; its owners and the two phase-1 owners are distinct.
The entry must receive current evidence before generating each checkpoint; its two decisions cannot be the same response.
This bound allows batched tool calls, relays and arbitrary legal rewiring. It omits discovery, requests, stale-copy checks, ratings, idle and extra model calls.
lowerBound.limitation: The meaningful bound is conditional on evidence causality, not an unconditional guarantee about arbitrary lucky model output. The unconditional host bound is only >=1 model response. Neither bound proves 120 seconds impossible, or that 10 calls suffice.
